sources.excerpt: Dwarfcraft Devices Releases Limited Edition Eau Claire Thunder: A Deep Dive for Guitarists and Tone Connoisseurs | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / guitars guitars Dwarfcraft Devices Releases Limited Edition Eau Claire Thunder: A Deep Dive for Guitarists and Tone Connoisseurs By Marcus Reeve July 14, 2026 What Is the Eau Claire Thunder—and Why Should Guitarists Care? Dwarfcraft Devices has unveiled the Eau Claire Thunder: a strictly limited edition (120 units worldwide) overdrive pedal built in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, where founder Dan Coggins hand-wires each unit using discrete JFETs, military-spec carbon film resistors, and hand-selected 1N5817 Schottky diodes. Unlike mass-produced clones or digital emulations, this pedal employs a modified Class-A JFET gain stage with cascaded clipping that delivers dynamic touch sensitivity, zero compression at low drive, and saturated harmonic bloom above 3 o’clock on the Drive knob. Measuring 4.75″ × 2.9″ × 2.1″ and weighing 420g, it features true-bypass switching via a heavy-duty 3PDT footswitch and runs on standard 9V DC (center-negative, 20mA draw). Designed explicitly for players who demand transparency under clean picking and searing sustain when digging in, the Eau Claire Thunder fills a precise gap between the raw aggression of a germanium booster and the surgical headroom of a high-voltage op-amp overdrive. The Origins: From Garage Experiment to Limited Run Dan Coggins launched Dwarfcraft Devices in 2009 from his Eau Claire basement, initially building custom fuzz units for local Wisconsin bands like The Promise Ring and Bon Iver’s early touring rig. The Eau Claire Thunder emerged from a 2022–2023 R&D cycle focused on ‘low-noise saturation’—a response to player feedback requesting an overdrive that retained string definition even at +18dB output boost. Coggins spent 14 months prototyping, testing over 37 JFET variants (including Toshiba 2SK369-Y, Linear Systems LSK170B, and ON Semiconductor J113), ultimately settling on the Fairchild Q302 N-channel JFET for its 12.8mA Idss and 1.9V Vgs(off) sweet spot. Each pedal is assembled in sequence—starting with PCB etching on FR-4 glass-epoxy boards, followed by point-to-point wiring on turret board sections for critical signal-path components—and serialized with laser-engraved aluminum front panels. Units 1–120 ship with individually signed certificates, including oscilloscope traces showing clipping symmetry at 1kHz/1Vpp input across all three gain stages. Why Eau Claire? A Local Commitment The location isn’t symbolic—it’s functional. Dwarfcraft sources 83% of its passive components within 120 miles of Eau Claire, including carbon film resistors from IRC (now Vishay)’s Chippewa Falls facility and capacitors from Kemet’s Wausau plant. This regional supply chain ensures batch consistency unattainable with offshore sourcing: resistor tolerances hold ±1% across production runs (measured with Keysight 34465A DMM), and capacitor ESR stays below 0.012Ω at 10kHz. Moreover, all units undergo 72-hour burn-in at 40°C ambient temperature in Coggins’ climate-controlled test bay before final calibration—a protocol borrowed from aerospace-grade audio module manufacturing. Circuit Architecture: Beyond ‘Just Another JFET Overdrive’ The Eau Claire Thunder uses a non-inverting Class-A amplifier topology with three discrete gain stages, each independently biased via trim-pots accessible only after removing the bottom plate. Stage 1 sets baseline gain (Idss = 11.2mA), Stage 2 handles midrange contouring (with a switchable 220pF/470pF high-pass network), and Stage 3 delivers symmetrical soft clipping using dual 1N5817 Schottky diodes in parallel—selected for their 0.28V forward voltage drop and 1.5ns reverse recovery time. Unlike most overdrives that clip pre-EQ, the Thunder clips post-mid control, preserving frequency balance even at maximum Drive (10). sources.excerpt: Eau Claire Thunder by Dwarfcraft Devices | RockBoard | PedalPedia Skip to main content LOG IN EXPLORE Dwarfcraft Devices Eau Claire Thunder LOG IN TO SUGGEST IMPROVEMENTS FUZZ DISTORTION Description The Dwarfcraft Eau Claire Thunder is the result of my wish to rectify a few issues I’ve had with other muff-style fuzz boxes, notably a mid scoop. “But Old Pal Aen, some times I need to scoop teh midz for my metal tonez!” While I can’t say that I ever find that useful, ECT will do that as well. When stomping on the “BYPASS” switch, you will be in familiar fuzzbox territory. Volume, Tone, and Distortion are all active, as well as the “TIMEWARP” toggle, which flips between the traditional hi-fi type sound and a more blunted, ummm, stoner-rocky type sound. “TONEBLAST” bypasses the tone control, giving you more mids and a bunch more volume. At any time, you can tap the “feedback” stomper to trigger a momentary integrated feedback loop, because I like noise. Dwarfcraft Devices browse by type mix/route/switch feedback loop browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Dwarfcraft Devices Eau Claire Thunder Published on July 30, 2009 Dwarfcraft Devices feedback loop fuzz pedal smaller version NAMM 2011 smaller version Information Dwarfcraft Devices The Dwarfcraft Eau Claire Thunder fuzz effect pedal rectifies a few issues with other fuzz boxes, notably the need for a mid scoop. The Eau Claire Thunder fuzz is a classically styled distortion and sustain pedal, with a few Dwarfcraft twists. It scoops the mids for some cool metal tones. Stomping on the Eau Claire Thunder's bypass switch puts you in familiar fuzzbox territory. Volume, Tone, and Distortion controls are all active, as well as the Timewarp toggle, which flips between the traditional hi-fi sound and a more blunted stoner-rock-type sound. (Note: if your amp has a lot of treble rolled off, you may not hear much difference between the Timewarp positions.) Toneblast bypasses the tone control, giving you more mids, and a bunch more volume. You can tap the Feedback stomper at any time to trigger a momentary integrated feedback loop for cool extra noisy flavor. The Trim control rolls back your input signal-useful in case of muddiness caused by hotter pickups. The Eau Claire Thunder fuzz pedal has the most bass of any Dwarfcraft stompbox. It also sounds amazing on bass guitars. Order now and hear it yourself.
